questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both that it had courses that I wanted and that it had Erasmus and was close to nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was overwhelming to navigate it all and be sure that everything was in order, but overall the information was accessible and I found everything I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got connected to a student adviser who could help with courses and if there was a scheduling issue and overall questions about uni

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were really lucky so for us it was easy, however I have many friends who found it really hard. I think most had luck on spareroom. We found our place at airbnb, we were 5 people looking together, which might have made it easier.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is hard to find, but our place was really nice. It is quite expensive, but so is the uni accomodations. It is important that you insist on paying the deposit through one of the government-approved schemes (e.g. SafeDeposits Scotland).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were lucky, however it is generally very hard to find something and quite expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The real course list came out a bit late, which meant that we had to change our OLA, and then register for courses again so it matched the OLA, but other than that it was fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, but I think I remember the process as okay intuitive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very! I got all the courses I wanted<3

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as early as possible when the right courselist comes out so you have better chances at getting the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was the same level as at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of it was the same, however we had more tutorials (holdundervisning?) and were fewer people in the tutorials. It was generally more conversation based than at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Feminist Debates
Religion and Society
Internet and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporary Feminist Debates was amaaaazing!!!!!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: HEating was much more expensive than anticipated/what we were told. Housing is generally really poorly insulated, so you either have to freeze or spend a lot of money on heating or both.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Heating and transportation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a society for EVERYTHING

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! a lot of both music, sport, and cultural soceities at the uni. You can find a club for any and all interests.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on the introduction hike with the hill walking society in the welcome week! generally go on a lot of hikes. I was a part of a really fun choir as well. There is also an erasmus society that makes trips around the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: hikes!! travel to the highlands, it is gorge! and go to a rugby game, find a pub quiz

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it is very close to danish culture I would say, so it was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is hard to bike, but otherwise nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: they are sososo sweet and welcoming!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not panick about housing or give up even though it is tough - most people found their apartments a week before ariving
Choose courses that are interesting to you
Join a society
